text.en: Raju saw a water tank shaped like a cylinder with a half ball on top. "How much water does it hold?" he asked.

The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder is 2 pi r h, its total surface area is 2 pi r (h + r) and its volume is pi r^2 h. A hollow cylinder has an outer and an inner radius, and the material used is found by subtracting the inner volume from the outer.
A right circular cone has curved surface area pi r l where l = sqrt(r^2 + h^2), and volume one third pi r^2 h. A sphere has surface area 4 pi r^2 and volume four-thirds pi r^3. A hemisphere has curved surface area 2 pi r^2, total surface area 3 pi r^2 and volume two-thirds pi r^3.
A frustum is a cone with its top cut off by a plane parallel to the base. Combined solids, such as a cylinder with a hemisphere, are handled by adding or subtracting the individual surface areas or volumes.

text.en: Paper wrapping covers a surface, while water fills a space. Use square units for surface area and cubic units for volume.

board.text: Area covers; volume fills

text.en: Cut an imaginary label vertically and flatten it. Its height is the cylinder height and its width is the circumference, two pi r.

board.text: A cylinder’s side unfolds into a rectangle

text.en: A closed cylinder has two circular ends. Add two times pi r squared to the curved area. For an open-top can, add only one circle.

board.text: Add the circles you can see

text.en: A circle of radius three has area nine pi. Stack that cross-section up by five units. The volume is forty-five pi cubic units.

board.text: Cylinder volume is base area times height

text.en: If a can measures twelve centimetres across, its radius is six. Substituting twelve for r would make the circular base area four times too large.

board.text: Measure radius, not diameter

text.en: For a tube of length ten with radii five and three, subtract nine pi from twenty-five pi before multiplying by ten. The material volume is one hundred and sixty pi.

board.text: Hollow tube: outer volume minus inner

text.en: Each ring-shaped end has area pi times outer radius squared minus inner radius squared. Count both rim faces if both are exposed.

board.text: An open tube has two annular ends

text.en: Vertical height is perpendicular to the base. Slant height runs along the side from the edge to the tip. They are different lengths.

board.text: Cone: distinguish vertical and slant height

text.en: For a cone of radius three and height four, the right triangle through the axis gives slant height five.
The same cone has curved area pi times three times five, or fifteen pi. If its base is exposed, add nine pi for the total area.

board.text: Use slant height for the curved surface

text.en: A cone has one third the volume of a cylinder with the same radius and vertical height. The cone with radius three and height four holds twelve pi.

board.text: Use vertical height for volume

text.en: Cutting a cone parallel to its base gives a round top and bottom of different sizes. The removed cone is similar to the original cone.

board.text: A frustum leaves a smaller circle at the top

text.en: If the original cone holds sixty cubic units and the removed tip holds five, the frustum holds fifty-five cubic units.

board.text: Frustum by subtraction

text.en: Double a sphere’s radius and its surface area grows by a factor of four. No flat circular end needs to be added.

board.text: Sphere area changes with the square

text.en: Double the radius and the volume grows by a factor of eight. Every linear dimension has doubled.

board.text: Sphere volume changes with the cube

text.en: Half the sphere surface gives two pi r squared. For the total surface area, add the exposed circular face, giving three pi r squared.

board.text: A hemisphere has a flat circular face

text.en: When a hemisphere sits exactly on a cylinder, their joined circles are inside. Include the dome’s curve, cylindrical wall and uncovered base in the outside area.

board.text: A dome and cylinder share a hidden circle

text.en: For the dome on the cylinder, add the cylinder’s volume and half a sphere’s volume. The parts share a face and do not overlap in volume.

board.text: Combined volume counts both parts

text.en: A hole removed from a solid subtracts volume. It can add exposed curved area to the boundary, so decide which surfaces are visible before calculating area.

board.text: A cavity can reveal an inside surface

text.en: If a solid is melted and all the material becomes smaller objects, equate the original volume to the total volume of all the new objects.

board.text: Recasting keeps the same volume

text.en: A sphere of radius four has eight times the volume of a sphere of radius two. Without loss, it can make eight smaller spheres.

board.text: Radius doubled → eight smaller identical spheres

text.en: If a cylinder radius is in centimetres and height is in metres, change both to one length unit first. One metre equals one hundred centimetres.

board.text: Convert units before substituting

text.en: For paint, look for exposed surface area. For liquid capacity or material in recasting, calculate volume. Check the units as well as the number.

problem.en: Find the volume of a cylinder with r = 7 cm and h = 10 cm (pi = 22/7).

text.en: V = pi r^2 h.
V = 1540 cubic cm.

problem.en: A cone has radius 3 cm and vertical height 4 cm. Find its curved area.

text.en: Slant height = √(3² + 4²) = 5 cm.

why.en: The radius and vertical height form the shorter sides of a right triangle.

text.en: Curved area = π × 3 × 5 = 15π cm².

why.en: Multiply by the slant height, not the vertical height.

problem.en: A hemisphere of radius 3 cm sits on a closed cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 5 cm. Find the outside area.

text.en: The cylinder’s side contributes 30π cm², and the dome contributes 18π cm².

why.en: The circles at the join are hidden.

text.en: Add 9π cm² for the exposed bottom to get 57π cm².

problem.en: A solid sphere of radius 6 cm is recast into equal spheres of radius 2 cm. How many are formed?

text.en: Divide the original volume by one new sphere’s volume. The common factor 4π/3 cancels.

why.en: Use cubic radii because volume scales with the cube.

text.en: 6³ ÷ 2³ = 27 spheres.

why.en: This assumes no material is lost.

prompt.en: A friend says The volume of a sphere is 4 pi r^2. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: The volume is four-thirds pi r^3.
